item.title: Q and A with Scott Anderson, Irrigation Extension Specialist with the PEI Department of Agriculture
item.description:
Q and A with Scott Anderson, Irrigation Extension Specialist with the PEI Department of Agriculture jenniferdhogan Thu, 08/06/2026 - 11:35

What is the role of the Irrigation Extension Specialist? 

I work with irrigators across Prince Edward Island to support effective, responsible water use while helping maintain healthy crop production during dry conditions. I can provide guidance on the irrigation permitting process, irrigation system planning and implementation, water-use efficiency, and irrigation best management practices. My goal is to help producers make informed decisions that protect water resources while supporting productive and sustainable farming operations.

What is your background? 

I grew up in Morell on a mixed farm of dairy and potatoes. I always knew I wanted a career in agriculture, but I was also passionate about pursuing a degree in engineering. I ended up combining the two and became an agricultural engineer. 

After I graduated, I worked with the PEI Department of Agriculture as a Soil and Water Engineer, and later with Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada as the Regional Water Engineer, where I worked a variety of research projects surrounding sustainability, crop analysis, and water management. 

Why are you passionate about this topic? 

With a background in farming, I’m invested in making sure producers who are interested in learning about irrigation are choosing the right systems for their unique operations and using these systems to maximize sustainability and profitability for themselves and their families. 

What would you like Islanders to know about this service?  

With climate change, we are going to have periods where we need another source of water on the farm, so that producers can continue to grow food for their communities and take care of their livestock. 

This role works in collaboration with growers, government, and other industry partners to make sure that irrigators are using water resources responsibly and efficiently. Water management and hydrology are resources. When used correctly, there should not be a shortage.

Who is this service available to? 

This service is available to anyone in the Agriculture industry across the island who needs technical support regarding irrigation. This could be any commodity – grains, vegetables, potatoes, berries, specialized organic farms - you name it. In just a few weeks on the job, I’ve already had the opportunity to visit a variety of operations, each one unique, which is why it’s so important to take the time to learn about the many facets of irrigation before you dive in! 

How can producers contact you about this service? 

Producers can reach out by email or phone at:  atlanticwaterpei@gmail.com or phone at (902) 916-0603. 

We’ll start by discussing your goals, ideas, and irrigation needs, then arrange a farm visit. From there, I can provide technical guidance, help you navigate the permitting process, and draw on my experience to support the development of an irrigation system that’s right for you.

item.title: Funding available to strengthen community and inclusion
item.description:
Funding available to strengthen community and inclusion jenniferdhogan Wed, 08/05/2026 - 11:23

Marking five years of investment in Island communities, the Gender, Equity, Diversity and Inclusion (GEDI) and Community Enhancement Program is now accepting applications from residents and community groups whose projects foster diversity, equity and inclusion across Prince Edward Island.

Since its inception in 2022, the program has invested more than $2,400,000 in initiatives that strengthen community engagement and encourage a greater sense of belonging across the province.

“It’s amazing to see the incredible projects that come to fruition year after year through this program. From cultural celebrations, and community arts, to BIPOC wellbeing and empowerment, this funding ensures newcomers and marginalized groups in PEI are empowered to shape supportive, diverse communities where everyone feels a sense of inclusion and belonging.”

-Minister of Workforce and Advanced Learning Zack Bell

Among the 2026 funding recipients was the Boys and Girls Club of Summerside, which received support for its Stick Together Festival. Delivered in partnership with Lennox Island, the festival welcomed Indigenous and non-Indigenous children, youth, and families from across Prince County to celebrate Indigenous culture, advance reconciliation and support cross-cultural connections.

"The support we received through the GEDI Program helped make our 2026 Stick Together Festival our most impactful event yet,” said BGC Prince County Community Engagement and Communications Coordinator Emma Harris. “It brought together more than 400 Indigenous and non-Indigenous community members for a day centered on inclusion, belonging, reconciliation, and kindness. We truly believe this event strengthened relationships within our community while creating a welcoming space where everyone felt they belonged.”

Applications can be submitted by email to GEDI@gov.pe.ca until 4:00 p.m. on September 23, 2026.

Learn more and apply here GEDI program.

item.title: Senior Islander of the Year Award nominations now open
item.description:
Senior Islander of the Year Award nominations now open jenniferdhogan Tue, 08/04/2026 - 15:45

Islanders can now nominate an outstanding older adult for the 2026 Senior Islander of the Year Award.

The award celebrates the many contributions of PEI residents who are 65 years and over and promotes positive aging. Examples of contributions may include community activities and engagement, volunteering, fundraising, education, research, fitness and recreation. 

"I encourage Islanders to think about the people who inspire them, strengthen their communities and make a difference in the lives of others. This award is a special opportunity to celebrate those contributions and recognize an older Islander who is truly deserving."

-Social Development and Seniors Minister Barb Ramsay.

For a nomination to be considered, the nominee must be:

  • 65 years or older at the time of their nomination and while making their contributions;
  • A resident of PEI both at the time of their nomination and while making their contributions;
  • Actively contributing to their community;
  • Willing to participate in the promotion of the award and related communications.

Past recipients and posthumous nominations are not eligible for consideration. 

In 2025, ten older adults were presented with a Senior Islander of the Year Award. They include Betty Dougan, Daria Valkenburg, Honourable Diane Griffin, Don Reid, Kit Loschiuk, Eileen LeClair, Estelle Bourgeois, John Rousseau, Dr. Umesh Gupta and Velma Bince.

To nominate a deserving older adult, visit: PEI Senior Islander of the Year Award. Nominations will be accepted until August 25, 2026.

item.title: New partnership will reduce wait times for MRI scans on PEI
item.description:
New partnership will reduce wait times for MRI scans on PEI jenniferdhogan Tue, 08/04/2026 - 12:51

A new partnership between the Department of Health and Wellness, Health PEI, and Building with Vision Ltd. will reduce wait times for Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans in Prince Edward Island and help improve access to this essential service for Islanders.

Through this partnership, patients referred by Health PEI will be able to receive publicly funded MRI scans at Building with Vision’s Summerside Diagnostic Imaging Centre.

“Reducing wait times and improving access to care are among our government's top priorities. This new partnership with Building with Vision will help more Islanders get the MRI scans they need, sooner and closer to home. By expanding publicly funded diagnostic imaging capacity here in the province, we are taking action to build a stronger, more responsive health care system for Islanders.”

-Minister of Health and Wellness Cory Deagle

A contract with an MRI facility in Moncton that started in the fall of 2024 has significantly reduced the backlog of patients waiting for scans. This added capacity closer to home will continue to help lower wait times.

“The Summerside Diagnostic Imaging Centre will allow us to continue to make improvements in our wait times and clear the backlog of patients,” said Laurae Klocschinsky, Interim CEO of Health PEI. “Even better, it will allow us to provide certain types of MRI scans closer to home. I want to be clear: this is publicly funded health care, using the capacity and innovation of our partners at Building with Vision.”

“My colleagues and I are pleased to partner with Health PEI in this important effort to help reduce MRI wait times for Islanders and improve health outcomes across the province,” said Dr. Guy Boswall of Building with Vision. “Timely access to diagnostic imaging is essential to ensuring patients receive the care they need, when they need it. By working together, we can help strengthen access to MRI services, support earlier diagnosis and treatment, and contribute to better care for patients and families throughout Prince Edward Island.” 

Patients will continue to follow the standard MRI process by being referred to the MRI department at Queen Elizabeth Hospital by a Health PEI health care provider. Patients cannot schedule their own appointment or be reimbursed for an MRI completed in a private clinic unless they have first been referred to a specialist who will review their case.

item.title: Province adds 60 long-term care beds in Summerside
item.description:
Province adds 60 long-term care beds in Summerside jenniferdhogan Tue, 08/04/2026 - 10:50

The Government of Prince Edward Island is expanding long-term care capacity in Prince County with a new 60-bed long-term care home that will be developed in Summerside.

Enhanced Living has been awarded the contract to build a private long-term care home that will help address the increasing need while improving access to care for Island seniors.

This project builds on government’s commitment, announced in the 2025 Budget, to add up to 175 new long-term care beds across the province to help meet demand and strengthen the health care system.

Through a 30-year agreement, the province will support the construction and operation of the new home, cover residents’ health care costs, and provide accommodation subsidies. Once the home opens, the province will provide up to $7.4 million annually to help offset accommodation costs for residents.                                           

This announcement builds on the recently announced 80-bed private long-term care home development in Cornwall. The added capacity will help reduce pressure on hospitals and supports Islanders who are waiting for long-term care. 

Government continues to plan for future long-term care needs and is advancing additional projects to expand access to care across the province. 

In Prince Edward Island, long-term care services are delivered through nine public and 11 private long-term care homes. With this investment, total long-term care capacity will increase to 1,465 beds.               

For more information, visit Long-term Care | Government of Prince Edward Island.            

Quotes:

“As our communities continues to grow, and so does the need for long-term care. This is an important investment that will help more Island seniors receive high-quality care close to home while supporting families across western PEI. It reflects our government’s commitment to expanding long-term care capacity and planning for the needs of Islanders today and into the future.”

- Premier of Prince Edward Island Rob Lantz

 

“We’re pleased to partner with Enhanced Living to expand care options in Prince County and help more Islanders access the support they need. Projects like this are an important part of building a more connected healthcare system that better serves seniors and families. This is another step toward ensuring Islanders receive the right care, in the right place, at the right time.”

- Minister of Health and Wellness Cory Deagle

"I'm pleased to see this important investment move forward for Island seniors and their families. Helping seniors stay connected to the people and communities they know and love, while ensuring they receive compassionate, high-quality care when they need it, is an important part of building strong communities across Prince Edward Island." 

- Minister of Social Development and Seniors Barb Ramsay

“Today’s announcement is welcome news for Prince County, and it will help more Island seniors remain closer to their communities. I’m proud to see Summerside continue to grow with the services needed to support Islanders’ health and well-being as they age.” 

- Summerside-Wilmot MLA Tyler DesRoches

"This is an important investment in both our community and the people who call it home. As Summerside continues to grow, so does the need for high-quality health care services that support residents at every stage of life. This new long-term care home will allow more older adults to stay close to the people and places they know best, while creating meaningful employment opportunities and further strengthening Summerside as a hub for health care in western Prince Edward Island. We look forward to seeing this project become reality."

- City of Summerside Mayor Dan Kutcher         

"The opening of this 60-bed nursing home in Summerside reflects a strong commitment to the community, ensuring more residents can receive compassionate, dignified care close to their families. As someone with deep ties to the area, I’m proud to be part of a project that will make a lasting difference in the lives of Islanders. " 

- Enhanced Living Director of Care Samantha Gaudet

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running.
